function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your network connection, so I can’t measure your speed myself. To find out what you’re getting right now, try one of these quick methods: | Method | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **Web Speed Test** | Visit a site like or . Click “Go” and wait for the download/upload results. | | **Command‑line (Windows)** | Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and run:
`powershell -Command "(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://ipv4.download.thinkbroadband.com/5MB.zip','C:\temp\speedtest.tmp');"`
Then delete the file. (This downloads ~5 MB; the time taken gives a rough speed.) | | **Command‑line (Linux/macOS)** | `wget --output-document=/dev/null http://ipv4.download.thinkbroadband.com/5MB.zip` – the transfer rate shown at the end is your speed. | | **Router UI** | Log into your router’s admin page (often 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1) and look for a “Status” or “Internet” section; many modern routers display current bandwidth usage. | If you want a more precise measurement, use a dedicated speed‑testing app or the official Speedtest app from Ookla, which will give you both download and upload speeds plus ping. Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the results!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "what is my internet speed". We need to respond. There's no tool to check internet speed. We can ask them to run a speed test or use an online service. But we can't actually measure. So we should explain how to check. Possibly provide instructions. Also mention that we cannot measure from here. So answer accordingly.
